selected_script.angle: dried muddy entryway footprints on worn hardwood where a regular wet mop lifts dirt but leaves a dull gray patch and visible fine scuffing
selected_script.hook: extreme close-up of dried muddy shoe prints on a hardwood entryway while a homeowner pushes a regular damp mop over them, but the dirty moisture turns into cloudy streaks instead of a clean shine

timeline.0-3s: Extreme close-up on dried muddy shoe prints and dull fine scuffs across warm brown hardwood planks by a front door; a regular damp mop passes over the marks, lifting some dirt but leaving cloudy streaks and a flat gray patch.
timeline.3-6s: The same damp mop keeps scrubbing the same area with more pressure; the dirty water smears along the wood grain, the scuffed dull patch looks wider, and the hand pauses in visible frustration while the floor still lacks shine.
timeline.6-10s: The DAXAXA Wood Floor Restorer & Polish bottle enters naturally beside the same dry cleaned patch; a small amount is applied to a clean flat mop pad and spread evenly in one direction, then a quick realistic jump cut shows the same area after drying with a glossier refreshed finish, fine scuffs less noticeable, and a side-by-side handheld tilt comparing the untreated dull edge to the treated shine while a natural spoken CTA says, “For worn wood floors, try DAXAXA.”

scenes.promptText: Create one complete approximately 10-second vertical TikTok-style UGC cleaning-product ad in 9:16, realistic handheld phone-shot style, natural home entryway lighting, no polished commercial camera moves. Use the provided product reference images as the exact product identity: DAXAXA Wood Floor Restorer & Polish 16oz, tall glossy red plastic bottle with rounded shoulders, narrow neck, ribbed blue screw cap, blue front label with yellow upper panel and cyan diagonal accent, small red DAXAXA brand badge, large Hardwood Polish identity, realistic label proportions, glossy plastic and printed label texture. Preserve product color, label, shape, material, size ratio, logo position, proportions, cap structure, and visible bottle structure; do not create a spray bottle or trigger nozzle. Timeline: 0-3s: extreme close-up at floor level of dried muddy shoe prints and dull fine scuffs on warm brown hardwood planks near a front door; a familiar ordinary damp mop passes over the mess, lifts a little surface dirt, but the muddy water smears into cloudy streaks and the floor still looks flat and worn. 3-6s: continue the same failed method on the exact same area; the homeowner pushes harder with the damp mop, the dirty moisture spreads along the wood grain, the haze and dull residue look more obvious, and the hand briefly stops in frustrated hesitation. 6-10s: the DAXAXA bottle enters naturally from the side and is set on the same floor beside the now-dry cleaned patch; a small amount of polish is applied to a clean flat mop pad and spread evenly in one direction over the same dull scuffed area, with real mop contact and no magical cleanup; include a quick believable jump cut implying drying time, then show credible proof with a handheld tilt across a clear before-after contrast: untreated edge remains dull and cloudy while treated section has a refreshed high-gloss reflection and fine scuffs look less noticeable. End with a light natural spoken CTA only: “For worn wood floors, try DAXAXA.” Keep product central and visible in the solution/result moments. Forbid UI, subtitles, stickers, text overlays, watermarks, captions, floating icons, diagram arrows, invented accessories, product drift, magical instant cleanup, exaggerated chemical reactions, smoke, sparks, bubbling, impossible mirror shine, or changing the product packaging.
